content.title: Phoenix Suns vs Los Angeles Lakers Live Stream: How to Watch NBA
content.text: The Phoenix Suns and Los Angeles Lakers will play a rare fifth game in this season’s series finale on Friday. The Los Angeles Lakers look to keep pace in the Western Conference standings when they host the Phoenix Suns in this season series finale on Friday night. It will be more difficult with Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves out until May 1 due to hamstring and oblique injuries, respectively. The Lakers ended a three-game losing streak since their stars went out with a win over the Golden State Warriors on Thursday. In the meantime, the Denver Nuggets leapfrogged LA for the third spot in the West, while the Lakers are now a game back. Phoenix is secure in the seventh seed, holding a three-game lead over the Los Angeles Clippers with two games left in the regular season. The Suns will still compete in the play-in tournament, likely against the Warriors. Phoenix won this series against the Lakers in its last game, beating Los Angeles 113-110 at home on Feb. 26. Royce O’Neale hit a clutch three with just 0.9 seconds remaining, after blowing a late 12-point lead. Doncic led all scorers with 41, while Grayson Allen led the Suns with 28, who were without Devin Booker. The Suns are slight 1.5-point favorites to extend their series lead to 4-1 on Friday. The Lakers ended their three-game losing streak on Thursday with a 119-103 win on the road against Golden State. LeBron James stepped up big, nearly putting up a triple-double with 26 points, 11 assists, and eight rebounds to lead Los Angeles in all three categories. The Lakers didn’t see Steph Curry, and they took advantage, breaking away in the second half to win the season series 3-1. Curry played in the Warriors’ last two matchups after missing 27 games, but Golden State didn’t play him on consecutive nights. Now it’s the Lakers and Suns’ turn to play on consecutive nights. The Suns are coming off a close 112-107 victory over the Dallas Mavericks on Thursday to clinch the seventh seed. Devin Booker went off for 37 points, and Dillon Brooks added another 28 to help earn the Suns the 3-0 series sweep. Phoenix was up 18 early in the third, but the Mavericks went on an 18-1 run to get back in the game, even though they had just 10 available players with much of the lineup out with injuries. Jalen Green was hurt in the matchup and is a game-time decision tonight with a knee injury. Booker will not be available tonight either, listed as out with an ankle injury.
